newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU fails to come up with 1996 grain crop estimate.
newsitem.headline: EU fails to come up with 1996 grain crop estimate.

text.p: The European Commission on Thursday was not able to come up with an official estimate for the 1996 grain harvest because it felt data provided by some member states may not be totally reliable, sources close to the EU executive said.

The EU's cereals management committee in Brussels met earlier to review the cereals, oilseed and grain legume crop data for 1996. The expert group was trying to make the first official Commission estimate for the new season.
But the Commission is apparently taking with caution the very high figures provided by some member states, sources said.
"If Brussels had added up all the data submitted by member states, it would have come up with a minimum of 195 million tonnes (for grain)," one source said.
But the sources said the grain harvest was likely to exceed 190 million tonnes.
On Wedneday a senior EU farm official said the crop may reach some 192 million tonnes.
In June an EU advisory committee had pegged the grain harvest at 185-187 million tonnes compared with 174 million tonnes in 1995.
